## Why the 1906 Earthquake Has Different Magnitude Estimates

One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories, then digitized and modeled usable data from 12. Its analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7 for the 1906 earthquake.

A USGS team took a different approach, re-evaluating geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake. Those measurements captured ground deformation through angles and distances between benchmarks, producing an estimate of 7.9.

The two estimates differ because they come from different methods of assessing earthquake size.
